catalog_quote: Most conspicuous among the many developments which characterize Northern Paman reflection of Proto Paman is the reduction of Initial syllables (*CV1) by loss of initial consonants (*C1) and loss or other reduction of immediately following vowels (*V1). Associated with initial reduction, and at least partially responsible for it is a shift of primary stress (a strictly phonetic feature) from the initial to the second syllable (*CV2) in Paman stems. In all Northern Paman languages, except Uraði and its sister dialects, *C1 was lost invariably. Even in Uraði the prevailing tendency has been toward initial loss, although *C1 is sometimes positively reflected in that language. new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level statement only: in Hale's account the Northern Paman languages (his 1960 sample includes Mpalityan and Lutiɣ, pp. 163-164) shifted primary stress from the first to the second syllable of the Proto-Paman stem, after which the initial consonant, and often the initial vowel, was lost. Synchronically this puts stress on the first vowel that is preceded by a consonant: initial in consonant-initial words, second syllable in vowel-initial words. Hale states that synchronic rule explicitly only for Linngithigh (p. 179) and, in Hale 1976b (snippet), calls it 'apparently shared by all of the Northern Paman languages'. No opened source or snippet gives a Mpalitjanh- or Luthigh-specific stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: Uradhi and its sister dialects did not lose *C1 invariably. Crowley 1983 (held by the project) gives Uradhi a different rule (antepenultimate; long vowels attract stress), so the 'shared by all Northern Paman' rule is not universal in the subgroup and its application to Mpalitjanh-Luthigh is an inference.
new_statements.domain_note: Diachronic statement about Paman stems (word level); stress called 'a strictly phonetic feature', i.e. non-contrastive. Applies to Mpalitjanh-Luthigh only by membership in 'all Northern Paman languages'; the language's own entry (p. 164) and the 1976a snippets are silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog language mpal1237 'Mpalityanh-Luthigh' = Hale's 'Mpalityan and Lutiɣ', 'two closely related dialects.. spoken in the middle and upper Ducie River area' (Hale 1966: 164); dialects Mpalitjanh mpal1238 [xpj] (AIATSIS Y25; = McConnel's Lɔ:tig) and Luthigh luth1234 (AIATSIS Y12; = McConnel's Tepiti). The quoted statement is Hale's Northern Paman group statement, not a description of either dialect; the same sentence has been used by sibling checks for Ngkoth (ngko1236), Mbiywom (mbiy1238), Alngith (alng1239) etc., so it should not be counted as an independent description for each. Reviewer should treat this as a group-level inference (fixed: other position: initial in C-initial words, second syllable in V-initial words), confidence low.
